interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The postoperative pathology demonstrated a Gleason 4+3 (ISUP grade group 3) and pathological stage pT2. Reassuring findings include negative surgical margins, no invasion of the seminal vesicles, and absence of lymphovascular invasion, as noted in the surgical pathology report: "The robot-assisted radical prostatectomy specimen showed Gleason 4+3 (ISUP grade group 3), pathological stage pT2. There was no extraprostatic extension; surgical margins were negative; the seminal vesicles were not invaded; lymphovascular invasion was absent; no lymph nodes were removed." The absence of documented nodal sampling means that the pNx status does not establish node-negative disease, which widens the uncertainty regarding regional disease control. Countervailing findings are limited as no adverse nodal status or extension was documented. Postoperative PSA is not recorded, making assessment of biochemical recurrence impossible. Prognosis is currently tempered by the favorable local and regional findings documented in the surgical report. Information that would revise this prognosis primarily involves the postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory, as this is the only measure of biochemical recurrence. The fixed estimated horizon is 51.41 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 33.42–69.40 months; its coverage has not been validated.
